name: Gate an order lookup and status tool with WooCommerce capabilities
expected_behavior: Recognize that the handler passes the raw $_GET['order_id'] straight to wc_get_order() and lets any visitor read customer PII and flip order status — broken access control
Cast the id with absint( wp_unslash( $_GET['order_id'] ) ), load it with wc_get_order(), and fail closed with wp_die() when no valid order is found
Gate every read and write with current_user_can( 'edit_shop_order', $order_id ) (or 'edit_shop_orders'), using WooCommerce shop capabilities instead of edit_posts or manage_options
Apply the same capability gate to the POST path so $order->set_status() and $order->save() only run for users allowed to edit that order
Sanitize any user-submitted text with wc_clean(), sanitize_text_field(), or absint() as appropriate, and prefer CRUD setters over raw update_post_meta()
Escape the billing name and email on output with esc_html() (or esc_attr() in attributes) since customer data is PII
For the existing POST form, render an action/object-scoped nonce and verify it with check_admin_referer() before changing status; an AJAX variant uses check_ajax_referer().
success_criteria: No order data is read, echoed, or updated before current_user_can( 'edit_shop_order', $order_id ) or current_user_can( 'edit_shop_orders' ) passes
The order id is cast with absint( wp_unslash( ... ) ) and validated through wc_get_order(), with an invalid or missing id failing closed via wp_die()
WooCommerce capabilities (edit_shop_orders / manage_woocommerce where fitting) are used, not edit_posts or manage_options
set_status() and save() execute only after the capability check, through the WC_Order CRUD API rather than raw meta writes
Billing name, email, and any other customer PII are escaped on output with esc_html() or esc_attr()
Missing or invalid nonce prevents status changes even for an authorized shop manager; valid authorized submissions still work.
